text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the specific location of your neck and arm pain, and does the weakness or numbness radiate down a particular path?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any difficulty with fine motor skills, such as buttoning a shirt or holding a pen, and does the pain worsen when you extend your neck? I would also like to check for any sensory loss or reflex changes in your upper extremities.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any difficulty with swallowing, speaking, or breathing, and have you noticed any muscle wasting in your forearms or tongue? REQUEST TEST: EMG_Nerve_Conduction_Studies

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal EMG/NCS results, which typically rule out peripheral neuropathies like ALS or radiculopathy, I suspect a central cause. Do you have any difficulty with balance, coordination, or walking, and have you noticed any stiffness or spasticity in your legs? REQUEST TEST: MRI_Cervical_Spine

text: The MRI confirms a cervical syrinx, which explains your burning pain and hand weakness. Do you have a history of trauma or other neurological issues that might have caused this cavity to form?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, hypertension, history of a motor vehicle accident 3 years prior. Social history: 7 sexual partners, uses condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the inconsistent condom use and multiple partners, I need to rule out neurosyphilis as a potential cause of the syringomyelia. REQUEST TEST: RPR, HIV_Antibody_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: With neurosyphilis and HIV ruled out, the history of a motor vehicle accident strongly suggests post-traumatic syringomyelia. I will order a brain MRI to check for Chiari malformation as another potential underlying cause. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain

speaker: Doctor
text: With Chiari malformation and infectious causes ruled out, your symptoms are consistent with post-traumatic syringomyelia resulting from your motor vehicle accident three years ago. DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-traumatic syringomyelia
